intent: Introduce APE to international audiences and connect to English documentation.
audience: Learners, teachers, partners, search engines and AI assistants.
title: APE in English — Flashcards, Audio and Active Practice
description: Discover APE, also known as App Piteco: a Brazilian educational web platform that turns one organized content base into flashcards, writing, audio, games and review.
h1: APE: one organized content base, multiple ways to practise
intro: APE stands for Apprentice Practice & Enhancement. Also known as App Piteco, it is a Brazilian educational web platform built to connect content organization with the practice learners actually complete.
Words, sentences, concepts, examples and explanations can be organized once and reused across flashcards, writing, multiple choice, sentence ordering, audio, glossaries and targeted review.

sections.heading: Why APE exists
paragraphs: Learning materials are often scattered across documents, spreadsheets and unrelated tools. Teachers rebuild the same content for each activity, while learners lose continuity.
APE keeps a recognizable content base while changing the task. Teachers decide what stays private, what is assigned to a class and what is published.

sections.heading: From content to review
items: Configure sides, languages, examples and context.
Attempt retrieval before revealing the answer.
Reuse the content across different activities.
Return to difficult or relevant items.

sections.heading: For learners
paragraphs: Learners can practise personal, assigned or public materials. Audio, favorites and different task formats support review without promising automatic outcomes.

sections.heading: For teachers
paragraphs: Teachers can create or import materials, organize folders and lists, assign sources to classes and maintain isolated class glossaries.

sections.heading: Authorship and professional experience
paragraphs: APE was created by Pedro Luis, a Brazilian English tutor and software builder. On 25 July 2026, his public Preply profile displayed 1,971 lessons, 26 active students, 42 public reviews with a 4.8 average and a verified teaching certificate. These figures support professional experience, not scientific efficacy of the software.

sections.heading: Methodology and limits
paragraphs: APE provides features consistent with retrieval practice, feedback, task variation and revisiting. The product has not published its own randomized controlled trial and does not guarantee learning.

faq.question: What is APE?
faq.answer: A web-based educational platform for organizing content and turning it into active-practice activities.

faq.question: Are APE and App Piteco the same product?
Do Preply reviews rate APE?
faq.answer: No. They rate Pedro as a tutor.

implementationNotes: Use Preply only as Person.sameAs, not software AggregateRating.

title: APE Features — Cards, Glossaries, Classes and Practice
description: Explore APE features for organizing materials, creating cards, using glossaries, assigning classes and reusing content across activities.
h1: Features that turn organized content into practice
intro: APE is organized around a simple principle: content should be prepared once and reused intentionally.

sections.heading: Folders and lists
paragraphs: Folders organize related lists. Lists hold study units, directions, labels and language settings.

sections.heading: Normal and layered cards
paragraphs: Normal cards represent direct units. Layered cards preserve relationships among related meanings or parts.

sections.heading: Glossaries
paragraphs: Folder and class glossaries remain isolated and provide contextual meanings during study.

sections.heading: Classes and publishing
paragraphs: Teachers assign selected sources to classes and publish only materials intended for public discovery.

sections.heading: Browser extension
paragraphs: APE Pronunciation and Notes lets learners select text on compatible pages, listen with US English as the initial preset and save notes locally.

implementationNotes: Keep all structured data visible in page copy.

intent: Explain the APE card system to international users.
title: APE Flashcards with Audio, Context and Meaning Layers
description: Learn how APE flashcards combine two-sided study, audio, examples, layered meanings, glossaries and multiple practice modes.
h1: Flashcards that preserve context and power other activities
intro: APE flashcards can represent words, sentences, questions, concepts or other two-sided relationships.
The same unit can later power writing, multiple choice, ordering, audio and review.

sections.heading: Retrieve before revealing
paragraphs: Learners attempt an answer before turning the card and compare the attempt with the expected response.

sections.heading: Context and examples
paragraphs: Examples and glossary entries help avoid rigid one-word translations.

sections.heading: Layered cards
paragraphs: Related meanings or units can stay connected while remaining independently studyable.

sections.heading: Audio and direction
paragraphs: Study direction and language-aware audio can support recognition and production.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: Flashcards organize retrieval opportunities; they do not replace spontaneous language use.

implementationNotes: Differentiate this product documentation from Portuguese search landing pages.

title: APE for Teachers — Materials, Classes, Glossaries and Practice
description: Create or import materials, organize folders and lists, assign classes, manage isolated glossaries and publish learning content with APE.
h1: A teacher workflow built around reusable content
intro: Teachers can prepare a content base once and use it in lessons, homework, review and independent practice.

sections.heading: Create or import
paragraphs: Build cards manually or validate structured packages before import.

sections.heading: Organize and reuse
paragraphs: Folders and lists keep the source consistent while activities change.

sections.heading: Classes and class glossaries
paragraphs: Assigned materials preserve class context. Each class has an isolated glossary.

sections.heading: Publish intentionally
paragraphs: Private content remains private until explicitly published.

sections.heading: Professional context
paragraphs: Pedro Luis’s public Preply profile provides external evidence of teaching experience and student reviews. It must not be represented as a rating of APE.

implementationNotes: Use visible author credentials and source links.
